title: Procurement Decision Canvas: Reserved GPU vs Hosted Token Pricing for Enterprise Workloads
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Purpose: Create a decision canvas and supporting dataset that helps Sales / Solutions / Procurement evaluate when a customer should be sold Reserved GPU (Dedicated) capacity versus hosted per-token pricing, given constraints around latency SLOs, predictable throughput, data isolation requirements, and cost budgets.

Goals:
- Produce a one-page decision canvas with clear thresholds (QPS, p95 latency, monthly token volume, data residency) for Recommended path: Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private.
- Back the canvas with a comparative cost model simulator and two enterprise case studies (finserv RAG search & HR LLM assistant).
- Identify top 5 competitive positioning messages and potential counteroffers (e.g., short-term burst credits, hybrid fallback routes).

Scope: Competitive pricing (public rate-cards and inferred reserved costs), SLA expectations, onboarding friction, and operational risk for regulated workloads. Excludes deep hardware procurement modeling (handled by Ops).

Deliverables:
1) Decision canvas PDF for sales enablement.
2) Spreadsheet cost simulator with toggles for batch size, token mix (prompt/response), KV cache hit rate, quantization delta, and burst policy.
3) Two annotated case studies with assumptions and recommended contract language.
4) Competitive brief summarizing 6 vendor approaches to reserved vs token pricing and observed tradeoffs.

Success criteria:
- Sales report a >50% reduction in time-to-proposal for customers with strict latency/SLA needs during the trial week.
- Finance signs off on model assumptions and variables.

Notes on approach: Combine public materials (competitor rate cards, marketplace listings) with primary research: 3 interviews with Solutions Engineers, 2 closed-won deal artifacts, and one customer pricing sensitivity survey. Use runtime telemetry to populate typical token mixes and p95 latency baselines for embedding vs generation flows.
acceptance_criteria: One-page decision canvas PDF uploaded to Confluence and Drive

Two enterprise case studies with reproducible assumptions and a checklist for legal/procurement
